description:
ABOUT MERCOR



Mercor’s mission is to organize human intelligence for the AI economy. We build the infrastructure that enables frontier AI labs and enterprises to train, evaluate, and improve AI on real-world professional work. More than five million experts have joined our network, and we pay out over $5 million daily for their knowledge and expertise.

We built our training and evaluation infrastructure alongside the world’s leading AI labs. Now, we’re bringing those capabilities to enterprises across industries, enabling them to train, evaluate, and improve AI using their own expertise and standards. Our APEX benchmarks measure how AI performs on economically valuable work, while our enterprise evaluations and post-training capabilities turn those insights into measurable improvements across real-world workflows.

Our work sits at the intersection of frontier AI, human expertise, and real-world application. We’re solving problems few companies have encountered, with the opportunity to influence what the world’s most advanced AI systems become capable of doing. We’re looking for people who bring different perspectives, take ownership, exercise sound judgment, and hold themselves to an exceptionally high standard. You’ll have the opportunity to do consequential work alongside talented colleagues who challenge one another, collaborate openly, and share a commitment to excellence.

Mercor is profitable and recently raised a $750 million Series D at a $20 billion valuation. We work in person five days a week in San Francisco, New York, and London.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Production Engineers at Mercor are software engineers who own the reliability, performance, and operability of the systems that run our business. You'll sit at the intersection of software and systems: writing code that automates operations, building the observability and deployment foundations every team depends on, and debugging the hardest problems live in production.

Our traffic and compute demands are growing fast, and the systems behind them (Kubernetes, Temporal, Postgres, MongoDB, and the gateway that fronts every model provider we use) need to hold up at the next 10x. You'll be the engineer who makes that true, and who makes deploys, alerts, and incidents boring.



This is a coding role. We expect you to automate your way out of toil rather than absorb it.


WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - Own the reliability program: define SLOs that matter, kill noisy alerts, and turn every incident into a durable fix rather than a runbook entry.

 - Design, build, and run our observability stack (metrics, logs, traces, and alerting) so any engineer can answer "what's broken and why" in minutes.

 - Own CI/CD and the deployment path to production: progressive rollouts, automated rollbacks, and a pipeline that lets an org shipping dozens of times a day (with coding agents as first-class users) do so safely.

 - Manage our AWS footprint and Kubernetes fleet through infrastructure as code (Terraform), with configuration management and change processes that scale.

 - Operate and tune Temporal, Postgres, MongoDB, and other stateful systems for performance, availability, and recoverability, including backups, failover, and capacity planning.

 - Design network and identity boundaries across production, preprod, and research compute, and keep Linux hosts and containers secure and well tuned.

 - Lead incident response: participate in a weekly on-call rotation, serve as an escalation point, run blameless site event reviews, and drive the follow-ups to completion.

 - Extend our AI-triaged, auto-assigned on-call: decide what gets automated next and build it.

 - Dig into data to find the root of a problem, then partner with product, research, and backend infrastructure engineers on the fix.

 - Make cost legible: attribute spend across cloud, data centers, and inference providers, and find the changes that bend the curve.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years in production engineering, DevOps, or infrastructure roles operating systems that real users depend on, and the scars to prove it.

 - Strong Linux and networking fundamentals: processes, memory, file systems, TCP/IP, DNS, load balancing, and TLS.

 - Advanced proficiency in Python or Go. You write tested, reviewable code to automate operations rather than relying on scripts and consoles.

 - Hands-on experience with AWS (for example EKS/ECS, EC2, S3, ALB, VPC, IAM) and infrastructure as code (Terraform preferred).

 - Production experience with containers and Kubernetes.

 - Deep experience with observability tooling (for example Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry) and with designing alerts people trust.

 - Experience building and running CI/CD pipelines at scale.

 - A clear model of how distributed systems fail: cascading failures, backpressure, retries and idempotency, and capacity limits.

 - Calm, structured incident leadership and the ability to work through ambiguous problems with engineering, security, and IT stakeholders.

 - High ownership: you see a gap, write the proposal, ship it, and carry the pager for it.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience operating Postgres, MongoDB, message queues, or workflow engines such as Temporal at meaningful scale.

 - Experience with GPU or inference workloads, or with multi-provider LLM traffic.

 - Security and identity experience: Okta, SSO, secrets management, least-privilege IAM, and provisioning automation.

 - Experience with chaos engineering, load testing, or disaster recovery exercises.

 - A track record of integrating AI tools into operational workflows with measurable results (faster triage, fewer pages, shorter MTTR).

 - Experience managing vendors and negotiating contracts, such as cloud commitments, observability or tooling licenses, and inference provider agreements, to balance cost, reliability, and flexibility.


HOW WE WORK

 - Small, senior team with direct access to the Head of Infrastructure and to engineering leadership.

 - In-person five days a week in SF. Infra is a team sport for us.

 - We use AI coding agents heavily and expect you to as well; the interesting work is deciding what they should do, not typing.

 - Weekly on-call rotation with structured handoffs. On-call load is a metric we actively drive down, and this role owns much of that work.
   
   Benefits

 - Bi-annual performance bonus structure

 - Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

 - Up to $15k Relocation bonus

 - $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

 - $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

 - Free Equinox membership

 - $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

 - $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

 - Health, Dental, Vision insurance

This Policy applies to all areas of employment, including recruitment, hiring, training, promotion, compensation, benefits, discipline, termination, and all other privileges, terms, and conditions of employment.
